Business Analytics and Intelligence (BAI) is the area of study that deals with skills, technologies, practices for efficient data management, continuous iterative exploration and investigation of business performance to gain insight and drive business planning.
There are an increasing number of BAI tools and methodologies newly introduced to the industry and academia every day.

These tools and methodologies provide field practitioners with statistical and operations analysis, the formation of predictive models, application of optimization techniques, and the communication of these results to customers, business partners, and college executives.
Business Analytics and Intelligence requires quantitative methods and evidence-based data for business modeling and decision making.
Business Analytics and Intelligence provide the industry with a great deal of benefits.
Data management solutions and analytical software continue to proliferate and provide better decision-making tools.
Businesses are increasingly relying on business analytics to gain a competitive advantage or just to keep up with the competition.
As such, students trained with BAI programs are highly-demanding future employees.
According to the U.S.
Bureau of Labor Statistics, Data scientist salaries in the United

States: $130,290 (2017), and Data scientist was ranked at #1 among 50 best jobs in America (Glassdoor.com).
Business analysts often specialize in a particular industry, such as medical science, telecommunications and energy.
Or, they may work in a specific area of business, like marketing, human resources or supply chain management.
In particular, those who are working for smaller firms may serve as general practitioners.
In all settings, the job of these professionals is to define a problem, collect and analyze data pertaining to it, evaluate company processes and procedures, and ultimately recommend and deploy strategies designed to solve the issue.
The Business Analytics and Intelligence program is to provide students with the opportunity to better integrate data insights into their analyses and decision-making process.
The program is also designed to strengthen knowledge from their primary major with advanced business analytics skills.
Students will be prepared to bring insights from the large amounts of data to their functional areas such as marketing, finance, supply chain management, accounting among others.

Students will specialize in one of the functional areas of business to gain additional skills that will prepare them for data-driven and analytics-based decision making.
Many of the courses of the program will be revised to include the important learning goals specific to Business Analytics and Intelligence.
Some courses listed in the COB curriculum will be tailored for BAI students.
The program will offer the courses of business statistics and mathematics, business application programming, data analytics software, e-Commerce, data management and visualization.
These courses were offered for the Management Information Systems (MIS) major in the college of business.

Half of the credits for the minor (3 courses) must be completed at URI.
All the courses for the minor must be taken at an AACSB accredited business school, at the URI Data Science program (CSC 201 or CSC 211) or through an approved study abroad program.

Marine Affairs URI’s Department of Marine Affairs offers the following degrees: B.A., B.S., M.A., M.M.A. (Master of Marine Affairs), and Ph.D.

Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages) The proposed program for an Online Graduate Certificate in GIS and Geospatial Technologies: will enhance and expand workforce development opportunities to a wider audience, fulfill a need for graduates with proficiency in highly sought-after geospatial technology skills including Geographic Information System (GIS), interactive map and data productions and field data collection. The online program delivery and accelerated online calendar provides flexibility to domestic and international students, working professionals, active and reserve service members to obtain meaningful, well-paid employment. Students completing this certificate will

2 have the 21st century skills increasingly expected by employers in the private and public sectors.
This program builds on the long-standing reputation of the University of Rhode Island as a national and international leader in the field of geospatial technology, particularly GIS.
The Environmental Data Center, a research lab in the Department of Natural Resource Science is considered the state's center of technical expertise in the field.
The power and timeliness of geospatial technologies is more apparent than ever.
Geospatial tools have driven the delivery of Covid-19 data to the public and decision makers.
Spatial patterns of the magnitude of outbreaks, dashboards (e.g., WHO) summarizing local conditions and visualizations of trends are all the result of geospatial technologies.
GIS Story Maps examining the history of transmission have appeared in the NY Times and other venues.
Geospatial technologies are used extensively across many sectors of the economy and are a critical support tool for resource management, planning, disaster management and mitigation, and community health, among others.

Increasingly, an expectation exists among employers that graduates will have working knowledge and understanding of geospatial technologies as they seek positions in the private and public sectors.
GIS is considered a high growth field, according to U.S Department of Labor and Statistics.
O- Net Online has compiled the data and found that employment in the GIS field is expected to grow 7 - 10 % faster than average, with 35,700 job openings in the U.S expected between 2018 - 2028.
Internationally, GIS analytical skills are highly sought after, and the certificate should be very attractive to students in developing countries.
Geospatial technology is rapidly evolving, and professionals are interested in expanding or acquiring the necessary skills to employ state-of-the-art techniques for collecting, analyzing, interpreting, managing, and presenting location-based data.

URI's recent market opportunity scan highlights GIS as a program with potential high student and labor market growth for expansion with recommendations to develop online versions of the GIS certificate (URI's Market Opportunity Scan; Hanover Research pg. 6) This proposed program complements undergraduate and graduate programs at URI in Natural Resources Science, Master of Environmental Science and Management and other related programs of study.
We anticipate significant interest for the program based on enrollment in the existing Graduate Certificate in GIS and Remote Sensing currently available to on-campus students.
An Online Graduate Certificate in GIS and Geospatial Technologies will allow learning opportunities for a wider audience and provide flexibility to accommodate and meet the needs of domestic and international students, working professionals, active and reserve service members and those seeking to acquire a powerful and practical skill set for employment.

The focus of the Online Graduate Certificate in GIS and Geospatial Technologies is two-fold: 1) to prepare students for opportunities in the expanding field of geospatial technologies and offer a workforce pipeline of graduates to meet the demand for geospatial analysts in the public and private sectors nationally and abroad; and 2) to facilitate enrollment and completion of the URI professional Master of Environmental Science and Management (MESM).
All credits associated with the Online Graduate Certificate in GIS and Geospatial Technologies can be used to satisfy a portion of the requirements of the MESM degree.
The certificate will follow the accelerated online academic calendar and include four 7-week courses (3 credits each) that develop core competencies in geospatial technologies: data creation, data acquisition, spatial analysis, data management and data visualization with maps and interactive applications.
The courses will focus on tools and technologies available within the Esri ArcGIS Desktop & Online platforms, considered to be the cross-industry standard for everything geospatial.

Course format and learning activities will emphasize critical spatial analysis techniques, data management and creative workflows for data analysis, capture and presentation, critical skills for modern day geospatial analysts and managers at all levels.
Upon completion of the Online Graduate Certificate in GIS and Geospatial Technologies, students will: 1) Will have advanced-level technical skills necessary to use geospatial data to address location-based challenges across disciplines.
We expect 10 - 20 students to enroll in the certificate program each year.
Applicants will be expected to provide 1) college transcripts certifying successful completion of a Bachelor's degree 2) two letters of recommendation from peers, mentors, or colleagues attesting to the student's ability to complete graduate level course work, and 3) a personal written statement explaining why the student is seeking a University of Rhode Island Online Graduate Certificate in GIS and Geospatial Technologies.
Accepted students will complete a sequence of four 3-credit classes for a total of 12 credits.
Since this is an online

3 program, the expectation is that it will be funded through revenues generated by the program itself and no other revenue will be needed.
